The Road South (Days 1–5)

GM page, with two read-alouds. Days 1 to 5: Loftwick down the Wool Road to Stell, and on toward the Sheldomar bottom-land. Run it as a montage: a read-aloud, a question or two round the table, and on to the Ford. The morning they ride out is Phase 2's @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-2-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P2DepartreJrn.JournalEntryPage.BR2P2DpPgEndRdAl]{Ending Read-Aloud — Departing East}; start after it.

Read aloud — the Wool Road

Days 1 to 3. About forty seconds.

The Wool Road runs south out of the Yeomanry the way a column of figures runs down a ledger: straight, careful, and in no hurry at all. Hedged fields, then open downland, then fields again, each with its stone barn and its watchful dog. Your cart creaks under its bales of samples. Carters going north lift a hand as they pass, and the hand says: buyers, then, and late in the season for it.

On the third evening the road comes down into Stell, a market town with one good inn and a great many opinions about the weather. Beyond it the land opens out and falls away to the south, toward the river, and Keoland.

Read aloud — Hennet Vole

Day 4, at a toll bar south of Stell. About a minute. Sev is named here on purpose; see the GM notes.

On the fourth morning you hear Hennet Vole before you see him: a voice going steadily at the head of a string of ox-carts drawn up at a toll bar, explaining to the toll-keeper, the toll-keeper's wife and an indifferent ox exactly what is wrong with the toll.

He is a broad, sunburnt man in a felt hat with four carts of fleeces bound for the Gradsul autumn market, three drovers, a boy who never speaks, and eleven oxen whose names he will tell you whether you ask or not. He takes one look at five armed travellers with a sample cart and attaches himself to you like a burr.

By noon you know the price of fleece in three counties and which of his drovers cannot be trusted with ale. That one is Sev, who has decided that the way one of you talks is the funniest thing he has heard all year, and says so, often.

By the second night, sharing his fire and his terrible tea, it is hard to remember the road without him.

GM notes

  • Why Vole is here. He is the witness the @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgTally00]{visibility tally} needs: everything the party does at the Ford, he will tell in the Gradsul market. See @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1NpcsJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1NpPgVole000]{his page} and @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-actors.Actor.BR2T1ActVole0000]{his sheet}. He is not a plant and nothing he says is a lie.
  • Sev is laughing at Gianni's accent. Name him now and let him be likeable. If he dies at the Ford it lands only if the table has heard his name for two days; if he lives, he says goodbye to Gianni on the Gradsul quay in what he swears is her own accent.
  • A question for the table. One answer each is plenty: what does your character do with a long, empty road? Whatever they say is what they are doing when the oxen stop on Day 6.
  • The Brown Hare. If the party ran the Sign of the Brown Hare sidequest, they pass the roadhouse on this stretch. Describe it as they left it.
  • Nothing has to happen here. No beat fires and nothing is load-bearing; if the table is impatient, read the first read-aloud and go straight to @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1FordJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1FdPgSetup00]{the Ford}, and let Vole introduce himself there.

The Fallow Ford

Day 6. Three days past Stell, where the Wool Road drops into the Sheldomar bottom-land and joins the Keoish cart road. Late afternoon. Fallow stubble, a drainage ditch along the east side, an ox-ford ahead. The Dreadwood is a green line on the western horizon and everyone on the road mentions it and nobody means anything by it.

Who is on the road with them

The party is travelling as a wool-buying delegation, which means they are travelling the way one actually does: their own cart of samples and letters, and four more carts belonging to @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-actors.Actor.BR2T1ActVole0000]{Hennet Vole}, a real Keoish drover taking fleeces to the Gradsul autumn market, who was glad of the company and is paying nothing for it. Eleven oxen, three drovers, a boy of about twelve.

This matters for exactly one reason. There are witnesses, and the witnesses are going to the same market where the party will shortly be choosing a hull.

Read aloud

Read as Vole's lead carts come down to the water. About a minute.

Three days past Stell the Wool Road drops off the downland into the Sheldomar bottom-land and becomes something wetter and more patient: a cart road between drainage ditches, through fields gone to stubble and fields left fallow, under a sky that has been threatening rain since breakfast and has not yet troubled to deliver it. Far off to the west, low and dark along the horizon, lies the Dreadwood. Everyone on the road mentions it. Nobody means anything by it.

Late in the afternoon the road comes down to an ox-ford: a broad brown shallows where a stream crosses on its way to the river, a ditch along the near side of the road, and a fallow field running off beside it, all thistle and old stubble. Vole's lead carts are almost at the water.

The oxen stop.

Not shying, not baulking at the water — stopping. All eleven of them, heads down, and the lead pair in Vole's second string begin, slowly and with great determination, to back the cart up the road they came down. One of the drovers swears and goes to the bridles. The boy doesn't move at all.

Vole says, to nobody: “That's not the ford they don't like.”

The round before initiative

Give them one. Anyone who asks the animals or the ground: Survival DC 12 to read it as ground-sense rather than temperament — something under the field, moving, and the oxen can feel it through their feet. Gianni and Kitty get this free; a druid does not need a die to know what a frightened ox knows.

What they do with that round is the encounter's first real decision: get the carts turned (two rounds of work, and it saves the sample cart), or get bodies between the field and the oxen (and the carts stay where they are).

Then the first ankheg comes up under the second cart.

Read aloud — the first one

At the top of round one, once the party has used its round. The rest of the brood surfaces over the next two rounds at the hidden tunnel mouths, the old one last, north-east across the ford.

The second cart lifts.

Only a hand's breadth at first, at the near wheel, as if the road had taken a breath. Then the ground under it bulges, splits and comes apart in clods, and something comes up out of it all at once: a long armoured body the colour of old bone, too many legs, and a head that is mostly jaws. It takes the near ox by the foreleg.

The cart goes over with a noise like a barn falling down. Fleeces spill across the road. And out in the fallow field, in three places at once, the stubble begins to move.

The Ankheg Brood — Enemies & Tactics

Six ankhegs, one of them old. They have been feeding on this stretch of road all autumn, which is why it is empty at this hour and why nobody in Stell thought to mention it.

EnemyCountCRXP eachTotal
Ankheg524502,250
@UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-actors.Actor.BR2T1ActAnkElder]{Ankheg Elder}, the old one — +20 hp, acid spray recharges on 5–612450450
Encounter total2,700 XP

Six PCs: a seventh ankheg (+450).

Where the sheets come from. The old one ships as @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-actors.Actor.BR2T1ActAnkElder]{Ankheg Elder} in First Travel Intermission — NPCs, with the flat +20 hit points and the wider recharge window already on the sheet. Pull the other five from your monster compendium; the ankheg is SRD content and present in every monster set. Use whichever statistics your compendium actually has rather than a number written here, but check the Bite's damage type: the 2024 Monster Manual and SRD 5.2 print it as Slashing, and at least one compendium has it as Piercing. What matters mechanically is the shape: burrow, tremorsense, a bite that grapples, and a line of acid on a recharge.

How they fight

They are not hunting the party. They are hunting the oxen, which weigh eight hundred pounds each and cannot run, and an ankheg that gets a grapple drags toward a tunnel mouth rather than staying to trade blows. That single behaviour is what makes this fight interesting against a party with no front line: every grapple is a countdown rather than a damage roll, and every PC who goes to break one is a PC who is not killing anything.

The old one does not close. It surfaces at distance, lines up the longest row of bodies or the highest-value target it can see, and sprays. It targets the sample cart in preference to a person, because it is trying to drive the herd, not win a battle.

What beats them, and let it

An ankheg moves 30 feet and burrows 10. Spike growth or entangle across the field turns the brood into paper targets, and the first time Kitty does that to a burrowing monster she should get to feel clever about it for the rest of the voyage. Equally, six creatures at AC 14 standing in a stubble field is the best fireball target the party will see for a month — and taking it has a price that is not mechanical. See the visibility tally.

Terrain, the Cart Clock & Outcomes

The scene

Run this on @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnFord0000]{Intermission 1 — The Fallow Ford}: thirty by twenty squares at five feet, a hundred and fifty feet of road to the ford. It opens in the start state — nothing on the field gives the ambush away.

Five cart tiles sit on the road with the lead yoke at the ford; cart 2 from the ford is the party’s sample cart. Put two ox tokens beside each pole (any draft-animal sheet, reskinned).

Six tunnel-mouth tiles are already placed, hidden. You can see them; the table cannot. When an ankheg surfaces, toggle its hole visible. The first is under cart 2 — which is why that cart is the one that goes over — and the one north-east across the ford is the old one. Tip a cart by rotating its tile.

Three pieces of terrain, and no more

The ditch along the east side of the road is cover and an acid-break: a spray does not turn a corner, and a body prone in the ditch is out of the line. The ford is difficult ground, and ankhegs will not cross moving water — anything that gets over it is safe, and Vole's drovers will work that out on their own and start hauling oxen across it whether or not the party tells them to. The carts are the point of the fight.

The cart clock

Run three rounds. The encounter is not a hit-point race; it is a question about the second cart, which is the sample cart, and which is parked over a tunnel.

The samples are ruined if either of these happens: the old one lands a spray on the bales, or two ankhegs are grappling the same cart at the start of a round. That is not a disaster and should not be played as one. It is three days in Gradsul and about a hundred and forty gold buying replacement fleeces off a stranger, plus a story about why a wool delegation is buying wool on its way east to buy wool — exactly the sort of loose thread that gets repeated at a quayside. Let them pay it if they earn it.

Outcomes

Clean win, samples intact. Vole insists on paying them out of his own purse and they should let him; refusing a Keoish drover's debt in front of his own men is worse manners than taking it. He tells the story at the market as “the western buyers can handle themselves,” which is the best version of it for them.

Win, samples lost. Three days and a purchase in Gradsul, and the first crack in the cover: their letters of introduction describe a delegation carrying its own samples, and now the samples do not match the letters. A customs boy would not notice. A clerk of the firm would.

A PC dragged down a tunnel. The likeliest bad outcome, and it is a rescue rather than a death: the tunnels run eight or ten feet down and forty long, and a grappled PC is at the bottom of one, alone, in the dark, with an ankheg. Two rounds to reach them by digging or by following, and Elle is the only one who fits comfortably. Play the dark.

The tunnel has its own scene, @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-scenes.Scene.BR2T1ScnTunnel00]{Intermission 1 — The Ankheg Tunnel}: the shaft is top left, the feeding chamber bottom right, and a side branch runs off the bottom edge into the rest of the brood's workings. Put the dragged PC and the ankheg in the chamber and anyone who follows at the shaft. Token vision is on and the only light is the sun down the shaft, so a PC without darkvision is fighting blind unless they make light of their own.

Read aloud — down the tunnel

Read to the player whose character is dragged under, as it happens. The rest of the table hears it too, which is the point.

The ground takes you.

One moment there is sky; the next there is earth in your mouth and your eyes, a grip on you like a vice, and you are going down and sideways, fast, through a tunnel that fits the thing dragging you and does not fit you at all. Roots tear at you. The light behind you shrinks to a coin, then a button, then nothing.

It stops. You are somewhere wider, in a dark that smells of wet soil and vinegar, and the jaws that hold you are still holding you.

A drover dies if the party ignores the oxen entirely. Name him first if you intend to let it happen — he is Sev, he has been laughing at Gianni's accent for three days, and his death is what makes the party careful for the next five weeks.

Read aloud — when the field goes still

When the last ankheg is dead or gone under. Read the opening, then the bracketed lines that fit, then the close that fits.

The field goes still. A long way off a bird starts up again, as though it had only been waiting.

Vole walks the length of his carts with his hat in his hands, counting oxen out loud, the way another man might pray.

[If the samples survived:] Your sample cart is on its side in the road, filthy and whole. Two of the drovers right it without being asked.

[If the samples were lost:] Your sample cart is on its side in the road, and what is left of the samples is steaming gently where the acid found them. Nobody says anything about it for a while.

[If Sev died:] Nobody laughs at anybody's accent for the rest of the day. They bury Sev at the edge of the fallow field, and Vole says the words, badly, and does not stop to wipe his face.

[Close, if the samples survived:] When the counting is done he comes to you with his purse already open, and will not hear a word against it.

[Close, if they were lost:] When the counting is done he comes and looks at the ruined bales for a long moment, and says that he knows a factor in Gradsul who will sell wool to wool buyers without laughing, and that he will take you to her himself.

The Visibility Tally

This is the mechanism that connects the road to the sea. Keep it on a scrap of paper and do not explain it to the table, now or later.

Count loud acts during the Fallow Ford. A loud act is any spell with a visible area effect, any casting a drover can see and describe afterwards, a wild shape taken in the open, or anything at all that a man would tell a story about in a market tent.

Loud actsTierWhat Vole tells the market
0–1Quiet“The western buyers can handle themselves.” Steel, arrows, and a lot of shouting.
2–3MixedHe tells it with detail, including the blade Alicia carries, which people do look at.
4+, or any fireballLoudHe tells it for the rest of his life, and he tells it in the Gradsul market tents for three weeks while a certain sort of person is asking a certain sort of question.

The tier sets one line of the circular found in the second encounter and nothing else. The party never learns the rule existed; four weeks later they simply find out how well their disguise was working. There are three copies of the handout, one per tier; the @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1HandJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1HoPgIndex00]{handout index} says which to show.

Why it is fair. The conspiracy's Loftwick intelligence is genuinely thin — @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.phase-3-journals.JournalEntry.BR2P3ArrivalJrnl.JournalEntryPage.BR2P3ArPgGMBrief]{GM Brief — Phase 3 Purpose} fixes that at they suspect; they don't know — so everything specific in that circular has to have come from somewhere the party can identify afterwards. A drover at a wool market is a source they can reconstruct. An omniscient enemy is not.

Into Keoland (Days 7–11)

GM page, with one read-aloud. Days 7 to 11, down the Keoish cart road to the coast, Vole's carts still with them. Nothing has to happen here: it is the breath between the Ford and @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.travel-1-journals.JournalEntry.BR2T1GradJrnl000.JournalEntryPage.BR2T1GrPgCity000]{Into Gradsul}.

Read aloud — the road to the coast

Days 7 to 11. About forty-five seconds. Read the bracketed line that fits the tally.

Below the ford the country turns Keoish by degrees: the same fields, the same weather, and a different accent at every toll bar, each a little more pleased with itself than the last. The road fills up. Wool carts, grain carts, a lord's carriage that drives everybody into the ditch, a column of soldiers under the gold lion of Keoland marching north, who look at your party the way soldiers look at anyone who is armed and not in the army.

You sleep two nights in wool-houses: long barns that smell of lanolin and lamp oil, where buyers and drovers sit up late by the fire arguing prices, and Vole is in his element.

[Mixed or Loud:] At every toll bar, while the keeper counts the carts, Vole tells somebody about the Ford. He is getting better at it.

On the fifth day the river comes up alongside the road and stays there, wide and brown and busy, and the air changes. There is salt in it.

Beat — Gianni, quietly. At a crossroads on Day 9, a milestone has had one arm of its carving cut away: the old waystation it named is gone from the stone, recut so cleanly that the chisel marks still show pale. The same work as the Loftwick waymark. Nobody else at the crossroads has noticed, and the road it named runs off into a hedge. See @UUID[Compendium.blooming-rot-2.pc-threads.JournalEntry.BR2PcThreadsJrnl]{Per-PC Plot Threads}; never explain it.

GM notes

  • The tally is already set. Nothing on these days changes it; Vole's telling at the toll bars is the same story he will tell in Gradsul for three weeks.
  • If the samples were lost, the replacements are bought in Gradsul, not here: Vole knows an honest factor there, and the Kestrel Wife does not sail until Day 15 anyway.
  • If they want to ride ahead of Vole, let them. He catches them up at the next wool-house, hurt, and talks about it all evening.
